$comment: Markup and text in a Kotlin value written into HTML, judged by both editors alike: interpolate escapes markup held as a String, the text of an Html, a joinToString of Html and what elements { } gives as a String, and writes an Html as it is; markup a Kotlin template writes into interpolate's format is read as format. A case may give `constants`, the workspace's const val names.

cases.name: a value joined with + is marked as markup where it stands
cases.source:
fun f(q: String) = "

50% " + q + "

"

issues.message: Kotlin writes the value `q` into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, mark it with + in interpolate { }, which escapes it; if it is markup you built, declare it Html or wrap it in Trusted(...).

cases.name: interpolate escapes the text of an Html in element text
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(h: Html) = interpolate("

%s

", h.text)

issues.message: interpolate escapes h.text here, so the tags it holds are printed as text: it is markup held as a String. Pass the Html itself, join a list of Html with joinToHtml(), or wrap markup you built yourself in Trusted(...).

", "x")

", if (b) "x" else "")

cases.name: markup from interpolate in an attribute is not told to use interpolate
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(x: String) = "

%s", x)}\">y

"

issues.message: Kotlin writes ${interpolate("%s", x)} into the HTML as it is, and it is markup: inside an attribute its quotes and tags are only characters, and a quote ends the value. Write text there rather than markup.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(x: String) = interpolate { "

%s", x)}\">y

" }.text

an Html a Kotlin template writes into the format is read as format

issues.message: Kotlin fills in $inner before interpolate reads the markup, so interpolate reads what it holds as markup too: a %s in it is a placeholder and a %% a per cent sign, and interpolate throws or changes the markup. Make it a %s placeholder and pass the Html: interpolate writes an Html or a Trusted there as it is.

cases.name: an Html in a braced template before a %s placeholder
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(h: Html, q: String) = interpolate("
${h} %s
", q)

issues.message: Kotlin fills in ${h} before interpolate reads the markup, so interpolate reads what it holds as markup too: a %s in it is a placeholder and a %% a per cent sign, and interpolate throws or changes the markup. Make it a %s placeholder and pass the Html: interpolate writes an Html or a Trusted there as it is.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate fun f(h: Html, q: String) = interpolate("
%s %s
", h, q)

cases.name: markup held as a String a Kotlin template writes into the format: no %s fix, which would escape it
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.html.* fun f(q: String) = interpolate("
${elements { b { +q } }}
")

issues.message: Kotlin fills in ${elements { b { +q } }} before interpolate reads the markup, so interpolate reads what it holds as markup too: a %s in it is a placeholder and a %% a per cent sign, and interpolate throws or changes the markup. Make it a %s placeholder and pass the Html: interpolate writes an Html or a Trusted there as it is.
